title: Febrile neutropenia (adult)
subject: haematology-oncology
setting: Emergency department, oncology or haematology ward, day care
summary: Fever (single oral 38.3°C, or 38.0°C for 1 hour) with ANC below 500 cells/mm3 is an emergency: cultures and an IV anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam within 1 hour, MASCC risk scoring (21 or more is low risk), vancomycin or antifungals only for specific indications, and oral outpatient therapy only for selected low-risk patients.

sections.title: Recognise and risk stratify
items: Fever: a single oral temperature of 38.3°C or more, or 38.0°C or more sustained over 1 hour. Neutropenia: ANC below 500 cells/mm3, or expected to fall below 500 within 48 hours (IDSA).
Signs of infection may be minimal. Hypothermia, hypotension, confusion or simply feeling unwell after chemotherapy may be the only clue; steroids can mask fever.

High risk (IDSA): MASCC below 21, profound neutropenia (ANC 100 or less) expected to last more than 7 days, or comorbidity such as hypotension, pneumonia, new abdominal pain, neurological change, severe mucositis, line infection, or renal or hepatic dysfunction.

MASCC score (maximum 26; 21 or more is low risk): burden of illness none or mild 5, moderate 3; no hypotension 5; no COPD 4; solid tumour, or haematological malignancy with no previous fungal infection 4; no dehydration needing IV fluids 3; outpatient at onset of fever 3; age below 60 years 2.

sections.title: First hour
items: Treat as an emergency: give the first dose of empirical antibiotic within 1 hour of triage (ASCO/IDSA 2018). Do not wait for the blood count in a febrile patient after chemotherapy.
Without delaying antibiotics, take at least 2 sets of blood cultures (one from each CVC lumen and one peripheral), urine culture, and cultures from any clinical site.
Resuscitate as for sepsis if hypotensive or lactate is raised. Avoid rectal examination and rectal temperatures.

sections.title: Investigations
items: CBC with differential, creatinine, electrolytes, liver function, lactate, CRP; chest X-ray if respiratory symptoms; C. difficile test if diarrhoea; respiratory viral PCR if coryzal.
Check previous cultures for ESBL, carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, MRSA or VRE colonisation: they change the empirical choice.
Fever persisting at 4 to 7 days in high-risk patients: CT chest, serum galactomannan, and review of lines, sinuses, skin and abdomen.

sections.title: Empirical antibiotics (high risk, inpatient)
items: Monotherapy with an anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam (IDSA): cefepime 2 g IV every 8 hours, or piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV every 6 hours, or meropenem 1 g IV every 8 hours.
ICMR 2022 (India, haematology and transplant units): piperacillin-tazobactam plus amikacin first line. Use a carbapenem for septic shock or previous ESBL infection or colonisation.
Unstable with known carbapenem-resistant colonisation: ICMR escalation is meropenem plus colistin or polymyxin B, with a glycopeptide and caspofungin; involve infectious diseases.

Add vancomycin (or teicoplanin) only for haemodynamic instability, pneumonia, gram-positive cocci in blood culture, suspected catheter infection, skin or soft tissue infection, MRSA colonisation, or severe mucositis on fluoroquinolone prophylaxis. Stop it after 2 to 3 days if no gram-positive infection is found.
Abdominal pain, neutropenic enterocolitis or perianal infection: ensure anaerobic cover (piperacillin-tazobactam or a carbapenem, or add metronidazole to cefepime).

sections.title: Low-risk outpatient therapy
items: Eligible: MASCC 21 or more (or clinically low risk), haemodynamically stable, able to take oral drugs, not on fluoroquinolone prophylaxis, with a caregiver, a telephone and quick access to hospital.
Give the first dose in hospital within 1 hour and observe for at least 4 hours before discharge (ASCO/IDSA 2018).
Oral regimen: ciprofloxacin 750 mg twice daily plus amoxicillin-clavulanate 500/125 mg three times daily; clindamycin 300 mg every 6 hours replaces amoxicillin-clavulanate in penicillin allergy.
Review daily by phone or in clinic. Admit if fever persists beyond 2 to 3 days, cultures are positive, or the patient deteriorates.

sections.title: Persistent fever, antifungals and duration
items: Persistent fever alone in a stable patient is not a reason to change antibacterials; change for clinical deterioration or a documented organism.

High-risk patients still febrile after 4 to 7 days of antibiotics with neutropenia expected to last beyond 7 days: investigate (CT chest, galactomannan) and start an antifungal: caspofungin 70 mg IV then 50 mg daily, or liposomal amphotericin B 3 mg/kg IV daily; voriconazole if invasive aspergillosis is likely.

Unexplained fever: continue antibiotics until the patient has been afebrile for at least 2 days and ANC is above 500 cells/mm3 (ICMR 2022). Documented infections: treat for the standard duration for that site and organism.
G-CSF is not routinely added for established febrile neutropenia.

sections.title: Monitoring
items: Vital signs at least 4-hourly; daily examination of the mouth, perianal area, skin and line sites; daily CBC and creatinine; aminoglycoside and vancomycin levels.
Reassess at 48 to 72 hours: cultures, response, de-escalation, and stopping vancomycin.

ICU referral for hypotension not responding to fluids, rising lactate, respiratory failure or altered sensorium. Remove the central line for tunnel infection, S. aureus, Pseudomonas, Candida or persistent bacteraemia.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Waiting for the blood count, or for the patient to look septic, before the first antibiotic dose.
Routine empirical vancomycin, or continuing it beyond 48 to 72 hours without a gram-positive infection.
Missing neutropenic enterocolitis, perianal abscess or C. difficile in patients with abdominal symptoms.
Oral outpatient therapy for patients already on fluoroquinolone prophylaxis.

drugs.name: Cefepime
drugs.notes: Anti-pseudomonal monotherapy; renal adjustment; no anaerobic cover.

drugs.name: Piperacillin-tazobactam
drugs.notes: Anti-pseudomonal monotherapy; ICMR pairs it with amikacin.

drugs.name: Meropenem
drugs.notes: Septic shock or ESBL risk; renal adjustment.

drugs.name: Amikacin
drugs.notes: ICMR combination partner; monitor levels, renal function and hearing.

drugs.name: Vancomycin
drugs.dose: 15 to 20 mg/kg IV every 8 to 12 hours (loading 20 to 35 mg/kg in critical illness)
drugs.notes: Specific indications only; AUC or trough guided; stop at 48 to 72 hours if not needed.

drugs.name: Ciprofloxacin plus amoxicillin-clavulanate
drugs.dose: Ciprofloxacin 750 mg orally twice daily plus amoxicillin-clavulanate 500/125 mg orally three times daily
drugs.notes: Low-risk outpatients not on fluoroquinolone prophylaxis.

drugs.name: Caspofungin
drugs.dose: 70 mg IV loading, then 50 mg IV daily
drugs.notes: Empirical or pre-emptive antifungal; 35 mg maintenance in moderate hepatic impairment.

drugs.name: Liposomal amphotericin B
drugs.notes: Empirical antifungal alternative; monitor potassium, magnesium and creatinine.
